title: Fourier coefficient of a leading-coordinate product
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $g:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, and let $S$ be a subset of the $n$ coordinates. Define a function on $n+1$ coordinates by multiplying the first coordinate by $g$ evaluated on the remaining coordinates. Its Fourier coefficient at the frequency consisting of coordinate $0$ together with the coordinates corresponding to $S$ equals the Fourier coefficient of $g$ at $S$.
hypotheses_covered: $g$ is a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube
$S$ is a subset of the $n$ coordinates
